summaries.demographer: Beulah Froneberger is a 19-year-old white, non-Hispanic woman living in Ringgold, Georgia, with her married parents and younger brother (Q51, Q88, Q89). She has never been married, has no children, and is not cohabiting with a partner (Q84). She completed high school and is currently enrolled in community college in a Visual Arts associate program while remaining financially dependent on her parents for housing and major expenses (Q90, Q91, Q55, Q83). Her household reflects working-class stability: her mother works in dental office administration and her father works in maintenance and warehouse-related jobs (Q103-Q107).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Beulah makes choices under tight financial constraints but is willing to accept uncertainty when it protects her creative identity, as shown by choosing visual arts and freelance commissions over more immediately stable work (Q02, Q16, Q83). She shows present-biased tendencies around procrastination, late-night work, and impulse spending on art or thrift supplies, but also uses low-cost substitutes, family support, and informal savings to manage scarcity (Q44, Q60, Q61). Her strongest incentives are autonomy, meaningful work, community recognition, and staying close to place rather than maximizing short-term earnings (Q65, Q108, Q109). Risk is moderated by living at home, avoiding student loans, and keeping education costs low (Q58, Q63).
summaries.political_scientist: Beulah is a newly registered voter who describes herself as an Independent closer to the Democratic Party, weakly attached to party labels but left-leaning on social issues, health care, education, climate, LGBTQ rights, and racial justice (Q23, Q24, Q95, Q96). She has limited direct law-enforcement contact and recognizes that her experience is shaped by being white and local to the area (Q20). She responds to Black Lives Matter through listening, discussion, online sharing, and attention to candidates rather than protest participation (Q26-Q30). Her civic orientation is community-based and localist, expressed through museum volunteering, trail club involvement, and concern that rural places be represented fairly (Q15, Q23, Q24, Q108).
summaries.psychologist: Beulah presents as curious, creative, place-attached, and somewhat disorganized, with strong openness to experience and a self-concept built around art, memory, and ordinary people's stories (Q01, Q65, Q109). She reports anxiety symptoms, especially around deadlines, money, and portfolio evaluation, but uses hiking, lists, yoga, friendship, and making art as coping strategies (Q43-Q45, Q50). Her relationships are close but selective: family provides stability and obligation, while friends provide emotional and creative support (Q05, Q07, Q44). She is in an emerging-adult identity phase, balancing Southern working-class roots, progressive influences, artistic ambition, and fear of impracticality (Q24, Q83, Q108).
